task: fracture-aware mechanics/material design and transport/dissipation in microstructured matter
overall_verdict: A conditional hydraulic-network certificate and an exact lubrication counterexample identify a precise missing interface: guaranteed transport after energy-bounded fracture/occlusive damage. The theorem is a standard path-conductance argument in a reduced model. The physical application, superiority, and novelty/priority remain UNKNOWN.

status_key.SOURCE_REPORTED: Statement directly supported by inspected primary-source content.
status_key.EXACT_WITHIN_MODEL: Derived exactly under listed reduced-model assumptions.
status_key.CONDITIONAL_DESIGN_CERTIFICATE: Mathematically valid if the measured graph and damage interface satisfy the listed assumptions.
status_key.INSPECTED_CORPUS_GAP: Not located in the inspected sources; not an exhaustive priority determination.
status_key.UNKNOWN: Requires physical evidence or a wider prior-art audit.

claims.exact_statement: For a thin Newtonian slit in the creeping-flow lubrication regime, two aperture layouts with identical fractions of aperture values b and a can have effective conductances G_parallel = W/(12 mu L)*(phi*b^3+(1-phi)*a^3) and G_series = W/(12 mu L)/(phi/b^3+(1-phi)/a^3), respectively. At phi=1/2 and b/a=10, G_parallel/G_series=250.50025; the ratio grows asymptotically as (b/a)^3/4.
assumptions: Thin rectangular slit, aperture much smaller than in-plane lengths.
Newtonian fluid, creeping laminar flow, no-slip walls.
Streamwise layout consists of parallel aperture bands; cross-stream layout forces every route through aperture bands in series.
Negligible side leakage and manifold resistance.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Counterexample: same compliance and aperture statistics, very different transport'
claims.novelty_boundary: The calculation is a standard lubrication-flow series/parallel construction, not a new flow law. It is an exact scope counterexample for predictors that receive only normal stiffness, porosity, mean aperture, or one-point aperture histograms. It does not falsify He et al.'s fitted relation within their simulated isotropic roughness family.
costs: Two-level microfluidic fabrication and pressure-flow measurement for a physical test.
Aperture mapping is needed to distinguish the layouts; scalar stiffness is insufficient.
claims.falsifier: For verified slit geometry and conditions matching the model, a measured conductance ratio far from 250.50025 would falsify the independent-slit approximation or reveal unmodeled side/manifold/lateral effects.
claims.next_gate: Fabricate matched streamwise-band and cross-stream-band chips and compare full normal force-closure curves and Q/delta-p.

claims.exact_statement: Given a finite passive hydraulic resistor graph with source s and sink t, pairwise edge-disjoint routes P_i whose conservative series conductances are each at least G_*, and conservative additive occlusion costs c_e, define B_cert=sum_i min_{e in P_i} c_e. Any occlusive edge set of total cost below B_cert leaves at least one complete route and therefore leaves effective conductance at least G_* by Rayleigh monotonicity. If the graph consists exactly of the listed disjoint routes and no other bypasses, B_cert is the exact minimum cost to reduce conductance below G_*.
assumptions: The reduced graph and terminal ports are supplied and fixed.
Each surviving edge has a valid post-load conductance lower bound.
Damage only deletes or occludes edges; it does not globally reduce conductance of surviving edges.
Each edge failure has an additive lower-bounded occlusion energy cost.
Fluid transport is passive and the network obeys a linear conductance law over the operating range.
claims.novelty_boundary: The path resistance formula, Rayleigh monotonicity, and edge-disjoint-path reasoning are standard network principles. The contribution is a scoped fracture-energy/post-damage-flow certificate interface; no general continuum theorem or priority claim is made.
costs: Acquire pore/throat graph, edge conductance lower bounds, occlusion/fracture energy lower bounds, and operating pressure range.
Verify listed routes in O(|E|) once a graph and paths are supplied; globally optimizing the architecture is outside the result.
Pore-resolved geometry acquisition and post-damage validation can dominate computation and physical cost.
claims.falsifier: A post-load conductance below G_* before the stated damage-energy budget, despite an independently verified intact route and valid lower bounds for every route edge, falsifies the reduced network assumptions or theorem implementation.
claims.next_gate: Validate edge-level conductance and occlusion-energy lower bounds on a same-batch microfluidic coupon, then test held-out damage sequences.

claims.exact_statement: In a constructed three-corridor network with two identical slit segments per corridor (w=0.5 mm, h=50 micrometre, ell=1 mm, mu=1e-3 Pa s), each segment has model conductance 5.2083e-12 m^3 Pa^-1 s^-1 and each intact corridor has series conductance 2.6042e-12 m^3 Pa^-1 s^-1. For G_*=2.5e-12 m^3 Pa^-1 s^-1, three edge-disjoint corridors with a 1 microjoule cheapest occlusion site each give B_cert=3 microjoule; below this budget one qualifying corridor survives, while at that budget all three can be cut in the exact-union graph.
assumptions: All dimensions and the viscosity are illustrative constructed inputs, not measured material parameters.
Each corridor is a series pair of slits, and the three corridors are parallel with no additional bypasses.
The designated weakest site in each route costs 1 microjoule to occlude; companion sites cost more.
claims.novelty_boundary: Illustrative arithmetic only; it is not a physical prediction for an existing material.
costs: No computational or experimental result is claimed; quantities follow from the closed-form slit and path formulas.
claims.falsifier: Not a nature-level claim; a physical test can falsify only the assumptions or transfer of this parameterized model.
claims.next_gate: Replace illustrative g_e and c_e with independently acquired measurements on a fabricated coupon.

claims.exact_statement: He et al. (2025) derive a dimensionless stiffness-permeability scaling from 3D DEM simulations of rough, shear-offset fractures and parallel-plate flow calculations; they exclude the low-porosity/high-stiffness region where disconnected voids make predicted permeability too high.
assumptions: Evidence scope is the inspected primary article text and figures description.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'What current primary work establishes—and leaves open'
claims.novelty_boundary: The present work does not refute their within-family result. It targets a broader connectivity and damage-budget guarantee not supplied by the inspected scaling law.
costs: Source study is computational; measured natural-fracture calibration is not established by this report.
claims.falsifier: Not applicable to the source-reported description; any extension to natural fracture prediction requires direct validation.
claims.next_gate: Compare connectivity-aware certificates with the source relation on held-out directional and near-disconnection geometries.

claims.exact_statement: Rivas et al. (2025) verify a coupled porous-flow/phase-field model against microfluidic pressure and velocity fields for a fixed, already-open fracture; the phase field is stationary during flow, so their validation does not test mechanically evolving fracture topology.
assumptions: Evidence scope is the inspected primary article text.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'What current primary work establishes—and leaves open'
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a scope distinction; the paper is a strong experimental flow-model baseline, not a failed model.
costs: The source uses chip fabrication, pressure sensing, PIV, and three-dimensional simulation.
claims.falsifier: A broader assertion that this source validates fracture evolution would be falsified by its fixed-fracture experimental interface.
claims.next_gate: Extend a matched microfluidic flow comparison to prescribed crack/occlusion sequences.

claims.exact_statement: Among the inspected primary sources, no result provides a lower bound on post-damage port-to-port conductance for every occlusive fracture event below a measured additive fracture-energy budget.
assumptions: Search is scoped to the primary studies cited in FINAL_REPORT.md and the local reports selectively read.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, sections 'Local route and scope', 'What current primary work establishes—and leaves open', and 'Claim status and next gate'

claims.exact_statement: For verified two-height thin-slit chips with aperture ratio 10 and high-aperture area fraction one half, changing high-aperture bands from streamwise-parallel to cross-stream-series predicts a 250.50025 ratio in conductance under the lubrication model, while an independent-column mechanical model predicts equal complete normal force-closure curves.
assumptions: The lubrication and independent-column assumptions of LAM-1 hold.
Measured aperture ratio and area fraction match the fixture.
Finite edge, manifold, and lateral elasticity effects are controlled or modeled.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, sections 'Counterexample' and 'Decisive tests and falsifiers'
claims.novelty_boundary: Proposed test, not performed. No physical result is claimed.
costs: Two-pattern microfluidic fabrication; aperture imaging; pressure-flow bench; calibrated normal loading and force/displacement measurements.
claims.falsifier: After confirming the prescribed geometry and correcting for manifold/edge losses, a conductance ratio inconsistent with the predicted value rejects the simple slit model for that design.
claims.next_gate: Fabricate matched chips and preregister flow and compliance tolerances.

claims.exact_statement: Transfer of the route certificate to real rock, concrete, scaffold, battery, or architected-material specimens is UNKNOWN because cracks can both open and close paths, damage costs may be history/rate dependent, and intact-edge conductance may change globally with loading.
assumptions: Real systems may violate the graph model's monotone edge-deletion, independent-edge, and laminar-flow assumptions.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Costs, conditioning, and model–nature boundary'
claims.novelty_boundary: No specimen was tested and no material law or application advantage is asserted.
costs: Needs 3D geometry/flow acquisition, mode/rate-specific fracture calibration, coupled loading/flow experiment, and held-out validation.
claims.falsifier: Same-batch held-out post-damage flow tests that contradict the certificate after all its graph and lower-bound assumptions are experimentally verified.
claims.next_gate: Test a small controlled microfluidic coupon first; do not transfer to bulk materials before it passes.

primary_prior.role: rough-fracture stiffness/permeability scaling; explicit disconnected-porosity failure region
fixed-fracture porous-flow phase-field model with microfluidic pressure/PIV verification
weak/strong-bond fracture metamaterial with full-field extrinsic dissipation
classic cubic-law flow prior cited in the 2025 fracture-permeability source

stages: Fabricate the same-material streamwise and cross-stream two-height slit patterns; verify aperture histogram and normal force-closure curves; measure Q/delta-p.
Fabricate a three-corridor microfluidic coupon with sacrificial occlusion sites; independently measure edge conductance and fracture/occlusion energy bounds.
Apply quasi-static loading under maintained pressure; record force/displacement, crack events, pressure, and flow; test the predicted route certificate on held-out damage sequences.
strong_controls: Single nonredundant route matched in solid fraction, initial normal stiffness, mean aperture, total conductance, and notch location.
Pore-resolved Stokes solve on measured post-damage geometry.
decisive_experiment.failure_observation: Flow falls below G_* before B_cert while at least one route remains imaged intact and all conductance/cost lower bounds were independently validated.
resource_accounting: microfabrication, manifolds, pumps, pressure/flow calibration, force/displacement sensing, microscopy/PIV, per-edge conductance calibration, fracture coupons, repeats, and uncertainty propagation

overall_next_gate: Run the two-height connectivity test and controlled three-route post-fracture flow test; expand primary prior search before making any novelty or external claim.
